subject: Hosted API evaluation follow-up - quickstart, endpoints, rate limits
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Chris Barnes <chris@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API evaluation follow-up - quickstart, endpoints, rate limits

Hi Chris,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier - appreciated you and Jenna's time. Quick recap of what we covered and recommended next steps so your team can start a Hosted API eval:

- Recommendation based on our call: start with Hosted API to validate integration and throughput. Dedicated/Private are good fit later if you need predictable capacity or VPC-only.
- Quickstart: you can spin up API keys and a sandbox project in the Console; sample curl and SDK snippets are in the quickstart doc.
- Endpoints: text-generation, chat, embeddings all available. We'll provide the exact base URL and model names to align with your latency targets.
- Rate limits: default sandbox has 60 req/min and 50 concurrent connections; production tiers vary. For your expected 500 rps, we'd recommend a Dedicated pool or an increased quota on Hosted (we can provision a trial boost while you evaluate).

Attachments: redwood-quickstart.pdf (quickstart + examples), rate-limit-matrix.csv (rate/latency tiers).

Next steps:
1) I'll create a sandbox project and invite your devs (Jenna) by EOD.
2) Jenna to confirm which endpoint(s) you want to test first (chat vs. embeddings).
3) We can set up a short tech sync with our integrations engineer if you want to test client-side batching.

If that plan sounds good I'll start the sandbox and share keys; otherwise tell me which pieces to change.

Thanks,

Aditya
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Chris Barnes <chris@acme-corp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Lee <jenna@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation follow-up - quickstart, endpoints, rate limits

Thanks Aditya - this is great and very clear.

A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- For the sandbox/quickstart, can Jenna use a shared org key or do you recommend per-developer keys? We need to keep logs tied to devs for debugging.
- On rate limits: your note about 60 req/min seems low - is that per API key? What's the concurrent connection limit for the production hosted tier?
- Also curious about streaming support for chat completions and whether we can test that in the sandbox.

Jenna is focusing on chat flows first.

Thanks,
Chris

Cc: Jenna Lee <jenna@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation follow-up - quickstart, endpoints, rate limits

Chris / Jenna - quick answers:

- Sandbox keys: recommend per-developer API keys (you can create them in the Console). We provide request-level attribution in logs (api_key -> request_id) so you can map activity to devs. If you prefer central key for CI we can do that too.
- Rate limits: sandbox default is 60 req/min per API key and 50 concurrent connections per org. Production hosted tiers start at 1,000 req/min and can be scaled; concurrency depends on quota and pool type. I've attached the rate-limit-matrix.csv with more detail.
- Streaming: yes, streaming chat completions are supported in Hosted and fully testable in sandbox. SDK examples in the quickstart show Node/Python streaming snippets.

I've provisioned a sandbox org and invited Jenna (jenna@acme-corp.com). You should have an invite link in your inbox - let me know if you don't see it and I'll resend.

Next: if Jenna can confirm she's able to run the chat streaming snippet, Marissa and I can schedule a 30m tech sync to look at batching/latency tuning.

Best,
Aditya

Hi Aditya,

Invite received and I ran the Node streaming example - works as advertised. A couple of actionable items from my side:
- I tested chat streaming for a 3-turn flow; avg latency (tail) was ~220ms for our prompts. I'll collect a small sample and drop it in the shared folder.
- I'd like to increase the sandbox concurrency to 200 for the next 48 hours to stress test client-side batching across 5 dev machines - is that possible?

If you can grant the temporary concurrency bump, I'll run the tests and then we can schedule the tech sync to go over results.

Thanks,
Jenna
